NS-1(iii) requires the driver to make at least one in-app call before cancelling; the timeline records 0 in-app calls, and the driver's own statement admits 'I did not call.'

The two chat messages (22:39 'Reached, grey Kia Niro, waiting at the pickup.' and 22:44 '5 min up, cancelling the trip') satisfy the message limb but cannot substitute for the missing call limb, so the cancellation was not preceded by the required contact attempt.

The 5-minute free wait had not elapsed before the driver cancelled: he tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:39:00 and cancelled at 22:45:00, 6 min 0 s later, and on the timeline the wait counted from arrival gives 6 minutes — but the driver's cancel message at 22:44 was sent only 5 minutes after arrival, i.e. at the earliest boundary, so any strict reading of NS-1(ii) (later of scheduled pickup time and arrival) is not clearly met.

The rider's complaint that 'he never called me' is corroborated by the system record of 0 in-app calls (F5) rather than being a bare assertion, so it is not outweighed by any contradicting system fact.
Because an NS-1 condition (the mandatory call) was never satisfied, the $5.00 charge must be refunded in full under NS-2 / §2.3, and NS-2 directs that the fee be voided when any NS-1 condition fails.

The driver also cancelled voluntarily at 22:44 while he was still at the pickup point 41 m away and within the 200 m radius, which is a driver-side cancellation for a reason of his own choosing under NS-3 rather than a chargeable no-show once the call condition failed.
The rider has 2 prior no-show cancellations in the last 30 days, below the 3-in-30-days threshold for NS-9, and this profile fact does not decide the current case.
The driver's account history (642 trips in 90 days, 1 dispute, 0 upheld) shows no repeat no-show finding against him, so no flag_account add-on is sought on this record.

The fare record shows no surge (1.0x) and only the $5.00 cancellation fee in dispute, so the refund sought is exactly the $5.00 fee plus the pre-existing $5.00 goodwill credit issue — i.e. fee_waived/refund_full of $5.00 only.

weaknesses: NS-1(i) and (ii) are comfortably met: F7 shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 22:39:00 only 40 m from the pickup (within the 200 m rule), F3 shows he stayed stationary 41 m away for 6 min 5 s, and F6/F4 show he cancelled 6 min 0 s after arrival — so the driver can honestly argue the 5-minute free wait had run.

F2 shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 22:38:40 with 6 min 20 s cumulative time inside the radius, so the rider's non-appearance is real and the only defect is procedural (the missing call under NS-1(iii)).

F11 (driver: '5 min up, cancelling the trip') and F13 show the driver did give notice and did message in-app, which the driver will use to argue substantial compliance with the contact requirement even though the call limb failed.

F17 records 2 prior no-show cancellations for this rider in 30 days, which the driver can cite as a credibility point and as nearing the NS-9 threshold, though at 2 it is below 3 and cannot decide this case.

F5 and F13 are the whole of the rider's winning point; if the court reads 'in-app message and in-app call' loosely, the driver's admitted messaging plus a stated verbal attempt (not in the chat record) is his best counter.

claims.assertion: The driver arrived at the pickup: he tapped "I'm Here" at 22:39:00 while 40 m from the pickup point, which satisfies NS-1(i)'s arrival condition (GPS within 200 m).
The driver's closest approach was 38 m and he was stationary 6 min 5 s at 41 m from the pickup, staying continuously within 200 m for 6 min 20 s, so NS-1(iv)'s continuous-presence condition is met.

The free wait had expired before he cancelled: cancellation came 6 min 0 s after recorded arrival and 8 min 0 s after acceptance, exceeding the 5-minute free wait counted from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival (NS-1(ii)).

The driver informed the rider in-app before cancelling: he sent 2 timestamped in-app messages, the first at 22:39:30 ("Reached, grey Kia Niro, waiting at the pickup.") and the second at 22:44 ("5 min up, cancelling the trip").
The driver made no in-app call before cancelling, as confirmed by both the timeline (0 calls) and his own statement; this is the one NS-1(iii) limb that is not met.
The $5.00 cancellation fee on record is the fixed NS-1 fee and no surge applied (1.0×), so there is no additional or inflated charge to refund beyond that fee.

The complaint that "he never called me" is accurate on the call limb, but the rider's parallel claim that the driver left/cancelled before she came out is contradicted by the GPS: he was stationary at the pickup from 22:38:55 until the cancellation at 22:45:00.
The rider has 2 prior no-show cancellations in the last 30 days, which is profile context for the pattern of this dispute (not a ground of decision in itself).
The driver has 3.9 years on the platform, 642 trips in 90 days and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, supporting his credibility on the arrival-and-wait account.

weaknesses: NS-1(iii) requires BOTH at least 1 in-app message AND at least 1 phone call before cancelling; the timeline records 0 in-app calls (F5) and the driver himself admits he did not call (F13), so on a strict reading the fee is voided by NS-2 and the rider will rely on exactly those facts to ask for refund_full of the $5.00 (F8).
The rider's complaint that 'he never called me' is corroborated by the system records (F5, F13), so that part of her account is credible and cannot be dismissed.

There is no traffic justification for any haste (F14 shows free-flowing Robinson Road at band 5, F15 no incidents, F16 fair weather), so the driver cannot argue that conditions forced him to cancel without making the call.
The 0.5-year-old rider account (F17) is a weak point only against the driver's 'habitual no-show' narrative, and profile facts never decide the case (RD-6/NS-9 principle).

Conceded: NS-1(iv) presence is met — F3 shows the driver stationary 41 m away for 6 min 5 s and F2 shows 6 min 20 s cumulative inside 200 m.

Conceded only in part: the 6 min 0 s from recorded arrival to cancellation (F4, F6) does exceed 5 minutes, so NS-1(ii) is met; but the driver's own 22:44 message '5 min up, cancelling the trip' (F11) shows he cut the wait at exactly 5 minutes, which does not excuse the failed call limb.

Accepted on the message limb only: F5 records 2 timestamped in-app messages (F10, F11, F12), so NS-1(iii)'s message requirement is met — but NS-1(iii) is conjunctive ('AND … at least 1 phone call'), and the call requirement is not met.
Conceded, and it is decisive: F5 records 0 in-app calls and the driver's own statement (F13) says 'I did not call', so NS-1(iii) fails and NS-2 voids the $5.00 fee (F8).

No dispute on the amount or on the 1.0× multiplier (F8, F9); the question is only whether the $5.00 (F8) may be charged at all, and because an NS-1 condition failed NS-2 requires refund_full of the whole $5.00.

Not contested that the GPS shows him stationary at the pickup (F3) — but this helps the rider on the one point that matters: he had ample time and free-flowing road (F14, F15, F16) and still never made the call the policy requires.
Profile only: F17 shows 2 no-show cancellations in 30 days, below NS-9's threshold of 3, and NS-9 states the profile never decides the current case.
The driver's record (F18) does not cure a failed NS-1 condition; NS-1 is a checklist, not a credibility contest, and one missing call voids the fee under NS-2.
Conceded as framed: NS-1 is conjunctive, and the call limb is the only one in doubt, so the fee rises or falls on NS-1(iii) alone.
Conceded: F5 records 0 in-app calls before cancellation and F13 records the driver's own admission 'I did not call', so the call limb of NS-1(iii) is not met on this record.

Conceded in part: the message limb is met by F10/F11 (2 timestamped messages, first at 22:39:30), but NS-1(iii) is written as 'at least 1 in-app chat message, AND at least 1 phone call', so messaging cannot cure the missing call.

The wait limb is met: F7 places the "I'm Here" tap at 22:39:00 and F4/F6 place cancellation at 22:45:00, 6 min 0 s later, and NS-1(ii) counts from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, so the 5-minute free wait had run before cancellation; F11's "5 min up" is the driver's own rounding, not a record of the clock.

points.response: Not contested: F5 and F13 show exactly what the rider says on the call point, and the driver does not claim the ride was not a no-show — he was stationary at the pickup throughout.
Conceded: with NS-1(iii)'s call limb unmet, NS-2 voides the $5.00 fee, and the driver does not ask the court to uphold a charge the clause does not permit.

Rejected on its own facts: F4 records the app reason as rider_no_show and F3 shows the driver stationary at the pickup from 22:38:55 to 22:45:00, so NS-0 routes this to NS-1/NS-2, not NS-3 — the defect is procedural, not a change of cancellation reason.
Agreed on the law: F17's 2 no-show cancellations are below the 3-in-30-days trigger, so NS-9 is not engaged and profile facts decide nothing here.

Consistent with the record: F18 shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, so no flag_account and no violation are sought, and NS-2's flag limb is not triggered because F7 places the arrival tap 40 m from the pickup.

The refund is the $5.00 fee only: F8 is the sole charge and F9 shows 1.0x with no surge, and the rider's complaint invokes no NS-8 facts (no evidence the driver failed to arrive or made no contact attempt: F6/F7 show arrival and F5/F10/F11 show his messages), so no $5.00 goodwill credit arises.
